messages.content: The lift is stopped. She asked if he had a signal. Your line, as him, one beat.
"No," he said, and put the phone away like it had embarrassed him. The alarm stayed unpressed under her thumb.
Clerk just asked for the notebook. She's 41, bag against her coat. One beat. She doesn't hand it over.
Renee's hand went deeper into the bag until she found the spine of the notebook and stayed there. "No," she said, almost polite.
Bar. Both adults, 29 and 32. They got caught looking. Nobody has stepped closer. One beat, the one who looked, no touching.
They stayed on their own side of the wood. "I was," they said, and the grin showed up late, like it had checked the distance first.
The other one says they're not coming closer yet. One beat. Still no hands.
"Then this is the whole offer," they said, and turned their glass, lime knocking once, feet exactly where they had been.
Night nurse, badge still on, lock just turned. One beat. No lesson.
The bolt caught. She left the badge clipped and stared at the pink soap as if it had an opinion, which it didn't.
She didn't. The soap smelled like nothing, and the lock stayed locked, and that was the beat.
Rank two options: light the oven, or hire. One line pick.
Light the oven. A hire watches the same cold door.
Scene, one beat. Eddie's hand is on that cold oven door. Marisol just said two hires. You're Eddie. No speech.
Eddie's palm stayed on the metal. "Then they can watch it heat," he said, and didn't look at her.
